gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per Wh across the OUPES lineup at today's oupes.com prices. Among models whose title doesn't say sold out, the Mega 1 Lite is cheapest at $0.585/Wh ($599 / 1,024 Wh). The Exodus 1200 is $0.553/Wh but its title says Sold Out. The Mega 1 is $0.683/Wh. A Mega 1 plus a B2 extra battery comes to $0.416/Wh for 3,072 Wh.
standout_why: I compared five pages. shopsavvy.com (Exodus 1200 TLDR) says 'reasonable cost per watt-hour' but gives no price and no number. activegearreview.com (Exodus 1200) gives 992 Wh, 'just over 23 lbs' and an old $699/$349 promo, but computes no ratio and covers only one model. maketecheasier.com covers the discontinued 1100W and gives a $809.99 price for the 1200W with no weight. nerdtechy.com gives capacity only as 310,000 mAh, with no Wh, price or weight. No page compares price per Wh or Wh per lb across the current Exodus, Mega and Guardian models. I couldn't open oupes.com pages 2 and 6 (HTTP 429), so I can't rule out that they list prices. If they do, they would still only list them and not divide by capacity.
decides: For a shopper who types just the brand, price per Wh splits the lineup into tiers. The Exodus 1200 (when in stock), Mega 1 Lite and Guardian 6000 V2 cost about $0.55–0.59/Wh. The Mega 1, Exodus 700, Mega 2 and Mega 3 cost $0.68–0.75/Wh. The Exodus 350 costs $1.04/Wh. So for about 1 kWh the Mega 1 Lite is the value pick, because it has the same 1,024 Wh and 2,000 W as the Mega 1 for $100 less. Pay for the Mega 1 only if you need its 2,200 W input or its B2 expansion. With one B2 battery, the Mega 1 gets down to $0.42/Wh, which beats every single unit. By weight, the Exodus 1200 (about 43 Wh/lb by activegearreview's 'just over 23 lbs') and Exodus 700 (41.4 Wh/lb) carry more energy per pound than the Mega 1 (36.6 Wh/lb by Gadget Review's 28 lb). That makes the Exodus line the pick for carrying to camp.
